_doc: Automatic play stats (0.102): when endpoint is set, the game sends this browser's run history (anonymous random player id, no personal data) to the collector Worker in collector/ after every run and once per session; the /analytics/ dashboard reads it back. Empty endpoint = nothing is sent. Setup: collector/README.md. collectorVersion (0.119): the collector/worker.js VERSION this build expects; the dashboard warns when the deployed Worker reports another (it is updated by pasting collector/worker.js into the Cloudflare dashboard). benchmarkPromptRoom (0.133): once a player's best room reaches this, the Great Hall asks them (once, until a result exists) to run the BENCHMARK (ui/benchmark.js). benchmarkPrompt (0.00201): that ask on or off (off 0.00201–0.00218; on again since 0.00219 for the phone testers, from room 6); the ?debug BENCHMARK button works either way. benchmarkSince (0.00219): a result from a build older than this does not count — raising it to the build being shipped asks everyone again (a new round of benchmarks). perf (0.00222): the frame-rate summary's judgments (core/perfMonitor.js summarizeFrames) — nearShare = how close to a standard refresh rate a run's average fps must sit to count as that rate (6%: a phone 4.5% under 60 whose busiest interval is a smeared plateau still reads 60), paceShare = the share of frames on a faster rate's own pace that makes it the display (15%: a 120 Hz display dropping to 70 fps; 10% let a wide iPhone smear read 90); the stats page's grading: goodShare = fps at this share of the display's rate is green, okFps = amber from here, red below; hzSince = the first build whose refresh-rate reading is trusted — before it the rate came from the fastest 10% of frames, a step high on jittered timestamps (120 Hz Macs as 144, 60 Hz iPhones as 90 / 75, every ordinary frame 'dropped'), so the dashboard grades such a row by its fps and hides its dropped share. report (0.00225): the device report (meta/perfReport.js) sent with the stats after every run and benchmark — runs = how many of the last runs' summaries it carries, stalls = how many stalls (frames of 100 ms or more) a recording keeps with their labels.
